clue.text: Spy cable twisted in secluded spots

indicators.note: twisted tells us the letters of the two words before it are wrung into a new order

explanation.surface: A spy's cable has been bent out of shape somewhere out of the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Byplaces are out-of-the-way or retired locations, the quiet corners a spy might favour.

clue.text: One adept with racket and ball in town

parts.note: Bjorn Borg was a champion tennis player
O is ball-shaped, standing for a ball

clue.text: Pair up left and right somehow active? One may be expecting a second

definitions.text: One may be expecting a second

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: A is the grammatical abbreviation for active

explanation.surface: Paired up left and right in some fashion, and busy, is the second one waiting?
explanation.definitionFit: A pluripara is a woman who has given birth more than once, so one expecting again has had a child before.

clue.text: Forego sleuth in grip of a need, troubled

indicators.note: in grip of means held inside the jumbled letters that follow
troubled means disturbed, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: tec is slang for a detective

explanation.surface: Give up the detective who is in the clutches of a disturbing need.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges the letters of 'a need', and 'in grip of' holds the sleuth inside them. Forego is the old spelling sense of going before, not giving up.
explanation.definitionFit: Forego here means to go before, which is what antecede means: to precede in time or place.

clue.text: Against limiting a disturbance? It's very hard

indicators.note: limiting means bounding on both sides, so the word for against encloses the rest

a stir is a commotion or disturbance

explanation.surface: Opposed to restricting unrest? That is a tough position.
explanation.definitionFit: Cast-iron describes something rigid and unbreakable, figuratively very hard.

clue.text: Carve king from two-master

indicators.note: from here means the king is taken away from the boat

parts.note: a ketch is a sailing boat with two masts
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Sculpt a king out of a two-masted ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to cut a design into a surface, a kind of engraving.

clue.text: Opening of Indian address, strident without lines

indicators.note: without means the lines are removed from the word

parts.note: strident means shrill
L is an abbreviation for line, so two of them stand for lines

explanation.surface: An Indian speech begins loudly but without any lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Shri is an Indian honorific placed before a man's name, like Mr at the start of an address.

clue.text: Something like 180 grains, returning plenty

parts.note: plenty means a lot

explanation.surface: A measure of about 180 grains comes back in abundance.
explanation.definitionFit: The tola is an Indian unit of weight equal to about 180 grains, used for gold and silver.

clue.text: Jock's drumbeat, heading northward from western Europe?

the UK lies to the north of the western European mainland

explanation.walkthrough: 'Jock's' marks a Scots word; Jock is a nickname for a Scot.

clue.text: 51 with king's company in soft fabric, reddish brown

clue.text: Bitter affront, not the first, placed over barrel

clue.text: Button-hole? Fit one round strap from below

from below in a down entry means the word is read upwards

parts.note: a rein is a strap for guiding a horse

explanation.surface: Tailoring a buttonhole by fitting someone round a strap from underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from below' reads the strap upwards in this down entry, and 'round' wraps the one about it. A buttonhole is also a flower worn there.
explanation.definitionFit: A boutonniere is a flower worn in a buttonhole, so the question mark marks the punning sense.

clue.text: Love enthralled by involved chanting, sweet talking

explanation.definitionFit: Gnathonic means flattering or sycophantic, after Gnatho, the parasite in Terence's comedy.

clue.text: Travelling to USSR is stirring

clue.text: Vintage product of vine, not new, from Scott's pen

not new tells us to drop the letter N, the abbreviation for new

clue.text: Right aboard Turkish boat, here's a double-ended pickaxe

clue.text: Referring to listeners, bill is short of extremes

clue.text: Part of mass, idea sung after arrangement (8, two words)

clue.text: Those in the tea business? Design cut short

clue.text: Doll that is lacking wittily pointed remark

clue.text: Cornish mineral making Bobby squint

clue.text: What makes bread bake twice in being served repeatedly (12, five words)

clue.text: Pill boxes? Number out of place in club

clue.text: Stop medic filling centre of diary
